name: DropZone
description:
Any element as a place to drop objects. `accept` filters by item type, `validate` and
`disabled` refuse items reactively ("List is full"), and `sort` makes it an ordered list,
row or grid of the Draggables inside it: they part to open a gap where the item would land
and close up when one is lifted out. `onDrop` hands over the object and the source and
target positions; apply it to your data with `applyDrop`, `moveItem` or `insertItem`.
signature: <T = unknown>({ id, label, accept, validate, disabled, sort, onDragEnter, onDragLeave, onDragOver, onDrop, appearance, render, className, children, ...rest }: DropZoneProps<T>): ReactElement<unknown, string | import("react").JSXElementConstructor<any>>

props.name: accept
props.description: Item types it takes. Default: every type. A zone always takes back its own items.

props.name: appearance
props.description:
outline: a dashed accent edge on zones that take the item, solid with a tint when it is
over them, danger for errors. fill: the tint only. none: nothing at all, so the zone does
not look like one; style it from `data-drop-state` or the render function instead.

props.name: children
props.description: The zone's content, or a function of its state ("Drop to add", the reason).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Refuse every item for now; a string says why. The zone reads as disabled.

props.name: id
props.description: Unique within the provider; the target id in drop events.

props.name: label
props.description: A short name for announcements ("Done column").

props.name: onDragEnter
props.description: The item came over this zone.

props.name: onDragOver
props.description: The index or verdict changed while over this zone.

props.name: onDrop
props.description:
The item was dropped here. Apply it to your data synchronously; the zone animates the
items to their new places. Return false to refuse (the item goes back), or a promise to
show the zone as pending until it settles. A rejected promise shows the zone in error;
reject with a `DropError` to say why. Your data is yours to restore.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render instead of a div (`<ul />`, `<section />`).

props.name: sort
props.description: Orders the Draggables inside it: they part to open a gap and close up when one leaves.

props.name: validate
props.type: ((drag: DragInfo<T>, target: { index: number | null; }) => DropVerdict) | undefined
props.description: A verdict on the item now and, for sortable zones, the index it is over. Re-evaluated when the zone re-renders.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes applied to the outer element for layout. Use the component props and theme tokens for its appearance.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value when using the component without controlling its state.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).
